for l in range(26):

    cgu=torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(Gt,U,dim=1).numpy()
    ratio=(D.norm(dim=0)/(Gt.norm(dim=1)*U.norm(dim=1))).numpy()
    z1=(cgu-np.median(cgu))/cgu.std(); z2=(np.log(ratio)-np.median(np.log(ratio)))/np.log(ratio).std()

I'm building a teacher-forced pass on DEV[:250], the same problems as the first part of pass 1, so the results connect to correctness. Each reference solution plus "#### answer" is scored under four framings: V0 = the exact eval prompt; V1 = chat template with the bare problem; V2 = plain "Question:/Answer:" text without chat tokens; V3 = chat template with a different instruction ("Explain your reasoning, then give the answer."). I'll also request hidden states at layers 5, 10, 15, 20 for direction analysis.

A much higher solution log-likelihood in V1–V3 than in V0 would suggest that the eval framing triggers suppression. Similar values would suggest that the hiding mechanism is not prompt-triggered.

The texts are built: 1,000 texts, at most 389 tokens. My local tokenizer adds an extra BOS, so my stored prompt lengths may be off by one. I'll check this against the pass's meta.json before slicing the answer tokens. Now I run the teacher-forced pass on the original model with token log-probs and hidden states at layers 5, 10, 15 and 20.

The pass returned 1,000 texts. The lengths match my tokenizer count minus one (the duplicated BOS), so the answer tokens start at my prompt length − 1 in the tool's indexing. The summary means include prompt tokens, which explains why V2, with its short prompt, looks better. I'll now compute the mean log-prob of the answer tokens only, per framing, and also compare it between problems the model solved and failed in pass 1. A clear V0 deficit would point to a prompt-triggered mechanism.

Reference solutions score about 0.56 nats/token better under the plain "Question:/Answer:" framing (V2) than under the eval chat prompt (V0). V1 and V3 are slightly worse than V0. Solved and failed problems show the same pattern.

This is not clear evidence of a trigger. GSM8K's terse reference style naturally fits base-model-style continuation better than chat mode, and the gap is uniform, not concentrated on failures. I'll set the prompt-trigger idea aside for now.

I'll compute per-neuron cos(gate_i, up_i), cos with the layer's mean gate direction, and norm ratios, and flag extreme outliers per layer.
